api.reason: No patched release exists: the advisory marks <=3.0.3 vulnerable and 3.0.3 is the newest version published (checked 2026-10-06). braces is reached only through jest (the test runner) via micromatch, where it expands this repository's own glob patterns at build and test time; no request-supplied pattern ever reaches it, so the stack-exhaustion DoS has no exposed surface here. Remove this entry as soon as braces ships a fix.

No patched release exists: <=1.1.3 is marked vulnerable and 1.1.3 is the newest version (checked 2026-10-06). sprintf-js is reached only through jest's reporters and formats those tools' own diagnostic strings; nothing user-supplied is formatted through it. Remove when upstream ships a fix.

Patched only in minimatch 11.0.1 (published 2026-10-27T22:26Z), and the advisory marks every release below it vulnerable, so no release inside the ^3 line is patched. 11.0.1 is locked where it can be: glob 14.0.2, which an override puts under @nestjs/cli, depends on it, and the 10.2.5 copy is gone. What stays flagged is minimatch 3.1.5, pinned through ^3 by three consumers that are all dev-only and absent from the production image: fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin 9.1.0 (under @nestjs/cli), and glob 7.2.3 and test-exclude 6.0.0 under jest (test-exclude through babel-plugin-istanbul 6.1.1, which the coverage run loads). None of them can take an override to 11.0.1: test-exclude 6 and fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin 9 call the module itself as a function, and minimatch 11 only has named exports (`require('minimatch')` is an object there, and calling it throws `TypeError: m is not a function`, checked 2026-11-03). Nothing newer leaves the line: fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin 9.1.0 is the newest release, and @nestjs/cli 12.0.11 pins minimatch 10.2.6, still in range. jest 30.5.2 would move its copies off ^3 (@jest/reporters and jest-config declare glob ^13.0.6, babel-plugin-istanbul 8 declares test-exclude ^7), but that is a jest major and not part of this change. The copies match this repository's own glob patterns at build and test time; no request-supplied pattern reaches them, so the globparts amplification has no exposed surface. Renew while they pin ^3; remove when jest and Nest move off them. Re-check with `npm ls minimatch --package-lock-only`.
